questions.q: What manual change put sql-prod-01 at risk in this case study?
options: The engineer changed the VM's region, breaking its network connectivity
While re-typing tags to fix casing, an engineer forgot to re-add the DoNotDelete tag
The engineer disabled the VM's backup schedule
The engineer intentionally deleted the VM
questions.explain: A routine tag-casing cleanup through the portal accidentally dropped DoNotDelete when the engineer retyped the VM's other tags.

questions.q: Why did the compliance script catch this the same night it happened, rather than days or weeks later?
options: Because the script was run only once, right before the change happened
Because it ran automatically from a pipeline on a nightly schedule, with no one needing to remember to trigger it
Because the engineer manually ran the script right after making the change
Because Azure automatically alerts on any tag change
questions.explain: Chapter 7's running-from-a-pipeline practice meant the check happened on schedule that night, independent of anyone remembering or being available.

questions.q: What specific rule, added to the Lesson 30 script, flagged sql-prod-01 as a violation?
options: Any resource missing a CostCenter tag is automatically deleted
Any VM that has been stopped for more than 30 days is flagged
Any resource tagged Critical is automatically restarted
Any resource tagged Tier: Critical must also carry DoNotDelete: true, or it's a violation
questions.explain: Thornfield extended the required-tags check with a production-specific rule: Tier: Critical resources must also have DoNotDelete set.

questions.q: What was the real danger the missing DoNotDelete tag created for sql-prod-01, even though it wasn't stopped at the time?
options: It would have been charged to the wrong cost center
It would have lost its network connectivity immediately
It was now one routine pause away from qualifying for a separate cleanup script that deletes stopped resources without that tag
It had no real risk at all since it was still running
questions.explain: A separate operational script (built on the Chapter 6 pattern) deletes stopped, untagged resources — the missing tag removed sql-prod-01's protection from that script.

questions.q: Which three Chapter 7 practices does this lesson specifically credit for catching the near-miss?
options: Manual code reviews, weekly team meetings, and a ticketing system
Running from a pipeline (not a laptop), source control for the compliance rule, and pipeline-managed secrets instead of a personal credential
Faster VM provisioning, cheaper storage tiers, and better naming conventions
Using Python instead of PowerShell, better tagging, and faster internet
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties the outcome to three Chapter 7 practices: pipeline execution, versioned/reviewed rule changes, and pipeline-handled secrets.
